other_failure_modes.name: Target Leakage
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses a date column (`date_first_booking`) that is inherently tied to the target to engineer features. Since users who do not book (target `NDF`) have missing booking dates, this feature perfectly leaks the target in the training set. Furthermore, by forcing this feature to 0 in the test set, it creates a massive distribution shift that will cause the model to predict `NDF` for almost all test users.

other_failure_modes.name: Invalid submission IDs
other_failure_modes.description: The script assigns integer loop indices to the `id` column of the submission file instead of the actual alphanumeric test user IDs. This will result in an invalid submission file that cannot be scored by the leaderboard.

other_failure_modes.name: Invalid multi-class target encoding
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes a scalar target encoding for a multi-class target by taking the maximum smoothed probability across all classes. This discards critical information about which specific class is most probable, mapping entirely different class distributions to the same scalar value.

summary: The agent successfully sets up a deep learning pipeline for multi-class classification but introduces a fatal target leakage bug by using the `date_first_booking` feature, which trivially predicts the `NDF` class in train and breaks test predictions. Additionally, the agent incorrectly constructs the submission file using integer indices instead of actual alphanumeric test IDs, which will cause evaluation to fail entirely. There are also notable flaws in the multi-class target encoding implementation and the use of a random train/test split that ignores the temporal nature of the data.
